title: Berry–Esseen bound on intervals
statement: Let $\{X_k\}_{k\in\iota}$ be a finite family of independent, measurable real random variables on a probability space. Suppose each $X_k$ has finite second moment, mean zero, the sum of their variances is $1$, and each has finite third absolute moment. For every real interval $I$, allowing any choice of open or closed endpoints and the whole line, the difference between the probability that $\sum_k X_k$ lies in $I$ and the standard Gaussian probability of $I$ has absolute value at most $2C\sum_k\mathbb{E}|X_k|^3$, where $C$ is the third-moment Berry–Esseen constant.
hypotheses_covered: Each variable has finite second moment
Each variable has integrable third absolute power
$I$ is a real interval, including the whole line
